findings.title: Generic vision-encoder-decoder export covers any HF VisionEncoderDecoderModel with a CausalLM inner decoder — Effort-L0 for breezedeus/pix2text-mfr unless the inner decoder needs new patching
findings.observation: src/winml/modelkit/models/hf/vision_encoder_decoder.py registers @register_onnx_overwrite('vision-encoder-decoder', 'feature-extraction') (VisionEncoderIOConfig over pixel_values → encoder_hidden_states), @register_onnx_overwrite('vision-encoder-decoder', 'text2text-generation') (decoder), and @register_composite_model('vision-encoder-decoder', 'image-to-text'). Dispatch is at the HF model level — VisionDecoderWrapper loads the full VisionEncoderDecoderModel and delegates to model.decoder polymorphically. Per-architecture field-name differences (decoder.d_model vs n_embd) are handled by _VedDecoderNormalizedConfig via Optimum's NormalizedConfigManager. PATCHING_SPECS bundles trace-time fixes for known inner-decoder positional-embedding ops.
findings.effort_tier_required: L0 (if inner-decoder family already covered by PATCHING_SPECS); L1 (if breezedeus/pix2text-mfr uses an inner decoder whose positional embedding trips up trace-time export and needs a new PatchingSpec)
findings.recipe_template: Same first-mover gap as marian: no encoder-decoder recipe ships under examples/recipes/. Generate via `winml config -m breezedeus/pix2text-mfr --task image-to-text`.
gotchas: Diagnostic step 1: open breezedeus/pix2text-mfr's config.json on HF and read `decoder.model_type`. If it is MBart / TrOCR / GPT-2 / a family already covered by PATCHING_SPECS, this is L0. If it's a new family, expect to add a `_patched_<family>_forward` function modeled on the existing entries.
VisionEncoderIOConfig pulls num_channels and image_size from `encoder.*` subconfig — pix2text-mfr's encoder subconfig must expose these or the NormalizedConfig lookup fails.
Like marian/bart/t5, the composite emits two recipe files (encoder + decoder). No template to copy.

findings.recipe_template: Historical failed candidate only; do not check in recipes pinned to an unloadable checkpoint. Use the validated `vision-encoder-decoder-004` checkpoint and composite recipe pair as the current reference.
gotchas: Methodology lesson: SKILL.md Step 1's Optimum-coverage probe + the composite-emit confirmation are both necessary but NOT sufficient — the producer must also verify the HF repo for this specific checkpoint follows the standard layout. This is a 4th gate (after probe + winml registration + `winml config` cooperation) that no diagnostic step currently covers. A pre-build `huggingface_hub.list_repo_files(...)` check could surface this in one call.

Independent of architecture: any contribution that names a specific checkpoint takes on the risk that the checkpoint repo's file layout doesn't match what AutoModel.from_pretrained expects. The risk is higher for community-uploaded checkpoints (the prefix `breezedeus/` is a community user, not an organisation that publishes standardized repos).

This is the SECOND counter-example to _meta-008's 'probe is necessary but not sufficient' rule, in addition to bart-003. bart-003 was a forward-time assertion failure; ved-003 is a load-time fetch failure. Both surface only after a real `winml build` attempt.

findings.title: vit-gpt2 image captioning resolves as an image-processor plus tokenizer composite with a 12-layer cached decoder
findings.observation: PR #1122 final candidate 4679e5062425c4ecc131ee5481af427e15198080, base 24cccfb23d6e3c3b93ae9bb94399c326cee8ecea, checkpoint nlpconnect/vit-gpt2-image-captioning at revision dc68f91c06a1ba6f15268e5b9c13ae7a7c514084, resolved recipe-free inspect/config/build to image-to-text with exactly two components: ViTImageProcessor -> fp32 pixel_values [1,3,224,224] normalized to [-1,1] for VisionEncoderWrapper, and GPT2TokenizerFast plus decoder_input_ids, encoder_hidden_states, decoder_attention_mask, cache_position, 12 past key/value pairs and 24 present outputs for VisionDecoderWrapper. The r17 structured recipe delta is empty for all four checked-in recipes. Resolved configs preserve export.compatibility.transformers_attention=eager, use opset 17, apply gelu/layer-norm/matmul-add/remove-isnan/merged-reshape optimizations, and leave compile null; FP32 has quant=null while FP16 uses mode=fp16 with fp16_keep_io_types=true and nodes_to_exclude=null. HTP metadata is precision-stable: encoder=86,389,248 parameters/167 modules/53 traced (31.74%), rooted at ViTModel; decoder=152,806,656 parameters/249 modules/147 traced (59.04%), rooted at GPT2LMHeadModel. The separate hierarchies prevent treating the composite as one fabricated graph.

findings.title: Composite parity is tight in both precisions despite a coherent token-8 branch, and bounded COCO Eval reaches L3
findings.observation: The final-head r17 identical-input composite harness closes the older decoder deferral. FP32 encoder cosine/max-abs=0.9999999999987006/2.913177013397217e-6, first-step logits=0.9999999999999822/4.9591064453125e-5, and all 24 present-cache outputs have minimum cosine 0.999999999999737 and maximum absolute error 4.76837158203125e-6. FP16 encoder=0.9999996043261942/0.0011739134788513184, logits=0.9999999929462833/0.022426605224609375, and all 24 present-cache outputs have minimum cosine 0.9999997403654044 and maximum absolute error 0.0062813758850097656. In both precisions, greedy generation matches through token index 7 and branches at index 8: PyTorch selects 'monitor' while WinML selects 'chair'; both finish a coherent desk/computer caption. Exactly one tester-owned L3 run was performed at final SHA 4679e5062425c4ecc131ee5481af427e15198080 on FP32 CPU using two deterministic streaming train rows from LIME-DATA/COCO-Caption2017 revision b14474455722b8c56eb7cdeb3f6be76fca1bba7a, with beams/crops/prompts=1, generation length capped at 32, five references/image, 2 processed, CIDEr=0.8427 and CER=0.6316. This is a two-sample functional smoke only, with no benchmark or representative-accuracy claim and no Eval claim for FP16 or another EP.

findings.title: Static Analyze finds clean encoder coverage but decoder cache/control-flow gaps on OpenVINO and QNN
findings.observation: Final-head r17 static analysis covered fp32 encoder 366 ops/11 types, fp16 encoder 368/12, fp32 decoder 777/22, and fp16 decoder 827/22. The embedded analyze_result.json in each build contains only a DML runtime_support=false row with empty classifications, so it is not used as EP support evidence; r17 instead retained 24 explicit provider/device rule JSONs and 08-analysis-summary.json. Encoder rule rows have no actionable partial/unsupported findings across NvTensorRTRTX GPU, OpenVINO CPU/GPU/NPU, and QNN GPU/NPU. Both decoder precisions expose the same actionable pattern: OpenVINO CPU/GPU/NPU marks Add unsupported; QNN GPU marks Concat and Gather partial plus LessOrEqual unsupported; QNN NPU marks Gather partial; NvTensorRTRTX/OpenVINO/QNN leave Where and ScatterND unknown. Component mapping retains graph-support regions as partial rather than falsely mapped: fp32 encoder 246 mapped +120 partial +0 unmapped; fp16 encoder 246+122+0; fp32 decoder 764+13+0; fp16 decoder 764+63+0. The issues localize to decoder cache/control-flow and support regions, not the ViT encoder or lm_head. These are static rule classifications, not accelerator runtime PASS/FAIL claims; VitisAI has runtime_support=false and empty classifications.

validated_on: nlpconnect/vit-gpt2-image-captioning @ fp32/fp16 encoder+decoder @ 24 explicit static NvTensorRTRTX/OpenVINO/QNN/VitisAI rule artifacts @ winml-cli 4679e5062425c4ecc131ee5481af427e15198080
SUPERSEDED ANALYZE PROVENANCE: static rule scan @ winml-cli 17b8002018d29991ce579e7012fa1ed2d09e0809

gotchas: Prioritize decoder cache/control-flow operators when planning accelerator work; the encoder rule rows are not the limiting surface in this evidence.
Unknown Where/ScatterND and unsupported/partial rows require capable-host runtime validation before any EP support claim.
